memory_update.text: For the restaurant customer-relationship chokepoint, prioritize PAR and VYX as underfollowed small-cap software/POS rails that map directly to loyalty, ordering, payments, and first-party data.

DoorDash should remain the reference aggregator anchor, but the alpha-hunt lane should focus on infrastructure vendors that let restaurants keep demand generation, customer identity, payment data, and dispatch orchestration closer to first-party channels.

Olo would have been one of the cleanest public-market mappings for this node, but current evidence suggests it was acquired by Thoma Bravo in 2025. Re-verify listing status before including in any public-company universe.

Need later-layer verification of customer concentration, net revenue retention, module attach rates, and actual restaurant revenue mix for PAR, VYX, and FOUR before treating them as durable chokepoint beneficiaries.

node: Delivery aggregators, direct ordering, loyalty, and first-party customer data
summary: This pass expands the universe around the customer-relationship chokepoint in restaurants: who owns app traffic, loyalty identity, ordering workflow, payments, and dispatch. The reference lane is DoorDash because it represents the high-attention marketplace and demand-aggregation side of the node. The underfollowed lane is more interesting for Serenity Layer 1B: PAR Technology, NCR Voyix, and Shift4 each sit in less obvious software/payments/POS rails that can help restaurants preserve direct ordering, capture guest data, or integrate delivery and payments without fully surrendering customer relationships to aggregators. Olo would normally be a highly relevant candidate, but current search evidence indicates it was acquired by Thoma Bravo in 2025, so it is treated as a coverage gap rather than a current US-listed candidate.
